concept.title: Read the caller-visible contract
paragraphs: Start with the receiver, input types, return type, and accessibility. A return type promises what a successful caller receives; it does not hide failure meaning.
Use IntelliSense one parameter or member at a time rather than memorizing a dense signature.

concept.title: Modern does not automatically mean clearer
paragraphs: Prefer the form that makes this business rule easiest to read and maintain. Older or more explicit syntax can remain the better teaching or production choice.
Compiler diagnostics identify unsupported language versions, inaccessible members, missing required values, and unsafe nullable paths.

lab.title: Pattern Matching and Nullable Reference Types
lab.objective: Use nullable flow analysis and pattern matching to describe known delivery states without unsafe dereferencing.
lab.startingCondition: Prerequisites: the .NET SDK, VS Code or another C# editor, and basic ability to run dotnet commands. No numbered session or optional module is required. Create exercises/refreshers/r4 from scratch.

steps.text: Step 1/12: Create an isolated console project with dotnet new console -o exercises/refreshers/r4. Do not add it to PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and do not edit TimeClock production code.
Step 2/12: Open exercises/refreshers/r4/Program.cs and remove only the template Hello World statement.
Step 3/12: At the top of Program.cs, add a comment naming the scenario: Describe optional package-delivery updates safely.
Step 4/12: Enable nullable analysis in the isolated project and declare DeliveryUpdate? update.
Step 5/12: Create sealed DeliveryUpdate record with nullable DeliveredAt.
Step 6/12: First write the older explicit if/else null-check form in comments.
Step 7/12: Create a switch expression whose first arm handles null.
Step 8/12: Add a property pattern that requires Delivered true and extracts a non-null DateTime.
Step 9/12: Add a non-delivered pattern and a discard fallback for incomplete state.
Step 10/12: Run null, delivered, and moving examples and observe that the compiler allows only proven-safe access.
Step 11/12: Build with dotnet build exercises/refreshers/r4 --configuration Release. Read any diagnostic before changing code.
Step 12/12: Run with dotnet run --project exercises/refreshers/r4 --configuration Release, then open Solution Reveal and compare every line.
